messages.subject: Percentange of phenotypic variance explained.
parts:
I worked with non parametric score based phenotype and I found a LOD score=3.37 for the trait of form (confidence intelval also). Can you explain me how can I find the percentage of phenotypic variance explained? I also did the effect plot and watched all videos in youtube but I was not able to understand.
Thank you in advance

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Percentange of phenotypic variance explained.
parts:
The only function in R/qtl that provides an estimated percent variance explained by a QTL is fitqtl(). But this cannot be used with a non-parametric mapping method.

Here's an example using Haley-Knott regression:

data(fake.f2)
fake.f2 <- calc.genoprob(fake.f2, step=1)
out <- scanone(fake.f2, method="hk")
max(out)

qtl <- makeqtl(fake.f2, chr=13, pos=28, what="prob")
out.fitqtl <- fitqtl(fake.f2, qtl=qtl, method="hk")
summary(out.fitqtl)

karl
